facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Leverage moved up because debt rose faster than EBITDA after the acquisition. Reported net debt to EBITDA was 2.50x at the end of 2024, 1.24x at the end of 2025 after the revolver draw was repaid and cash built, and 2.73x at September 30, 2026. The January 2, 2026 acquisition took about USD 391.845 million of net cash and brought USD 338.608 million of non-recourse funding debt, so carrying value debt rose to USD 865.841 million while last-twelve-months EBITDA reached only USD 277.174 million. For creditors the recourse claim is still the USD 600.0 million of notes, but the reported ratio now mixes recourse and non-recourse debt, which is why the company states 1.5x on its own definition. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Partner concentration is the main business risk and has already cost volume. Customers of the top three retail partners generated 54.8% of consolidated 2025 revenue and those of the top ten 77.0%, two partners each accounted for more than 10%, and two retail partners have failed since 2024 (Big Lots in September 2024 and American Signature in November 2025), so store closures cut Progressive Leasing volume and earnings independent of customer credit quality. facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: PROG is a financial technology holding company whose profit comes mostly from one business. Progressive Leasing leases durable goods to near-prime and subprime consumers through about 24,000 partner locations and websites, and generated 91.73% of nine-month 2026 pre-tax profit and 77.70% of revenue. Purchasing Power, acquired on 2026-01-02, sells goods to employees of employer clients through payroll deduction, and Four offers buy now pay later; with the small Other segment they supplied the remaining 22.30% of revenue. Leases run for a fixed term of up to 12 months and the customer may cancel at any time by returning the merchandise, so revenue visibility is about one lease term and earnings follow approvals and partner volume quickly in both directions. The working asset is lease merchandise of USD 511.293 million and capital expenditure is only 0.59% of revenue, so cash generation depends on keeping approvals, losses and partner volume stable; that supports debt service while volume is steady and weakens it quickly when it is not. facts.text: PROG is a listed holding company and no controlling holder is identified in the documents supplied, so no sponsor is identified that could support or extract value; Business & governance rates governance risk medium on behavior alone because the proxy statement was not supplied. The annual report says the parent depends on dividends and payments from subsidiaries, particularly Progressive Leasing, to pay debt, repurchase shares and pay dividends, which ties the notes to the earnings of the weakest-trending segment. The recourse debt is the USD 600.0 million of unsecured notes guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries that are not named; the revolver is borrowed by a subsidiary and guaranteed by the parent; and USD 272.0 million of asset-backed debt sits in non-recourse entities whose receivables are pledged, so on those assets noteholders rank behind the asset-backed lenders. facts.label: Revenue durability
facts.text: Progressive Leasing revenue is recurring within each lease term but discretionary, cyclical and concentrated. Volume grew 1.20% in nine months and 2.3% in Q3 on a larger e-commerce share, yet revenue fell 4.37% over nine months and 0.69% in Q3 because smaller lease portfolios entered each period; active customers were flat at 781 thousand against 784 thousand. Customers of the top three partners produced 54.8% of 2025 revenue (USD 1,320.3 million) and the top ten 77.0%, partner contracts can be renegotiated or not renewed, and two retail partners have failed since 2024, so a partner event is a step-down in volume rather than a gradual drift. Management attributes the pressure to cost of living, fuel prices and the war in Iran, expects tighter decisioning to keep pressuring volume, and has reduced its 2026 revenue and earnings outlook ranges. Purchasing Power and Four are growing but small: consolidated revenue ex Purchasing Power fell 0.86% in nine months, so the group's growth is acquired. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: The cost base is mostly variable with volume: depreciation of lease merchandise is 52.56% of nine-month consolidated revenue, so margins can be defended when volume falls, but write-offs and selling costs are less flexible. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital expenditure is small at USD 13.0 million in nine months, but the real reinvestment is lease merchandise, which sits inside operating cash flow. Reported EBITDA converted to operating cash flow at 62.66% in FY2024, 145.13% in FY2025 and 166.13% in nine months of 2026, a spread that comes mainly from working capital and tax timing rather than earnings: the lease merchandise balance fell USD 71.2 million in FY2025 and USD 97.7 million in nine months of 2026, releasing cash as volume shrank, and net tax moved from USD 46.068 million paid in the first nine months of 2025 to USD 14.614 million received in 2026. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 324.9 million in FY2025 and USD 373.1 million in nine months of 2026, and USD 309.5 million after buybacks and dividends. The USD 310.0 million of corporate borrowings was repaid and corporate debt is back to the USD 600.0 million of notes, but cash fell from USD 308.774 million to USD 108.917 million, so net recourse debt rose by USD 199.857 million over nine months; conversion of this size is not durable, because a volume recovery would absorb cash in inventory again. facts.label: Competitive forces, macro and regulation
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high: the annual report describes the virtual lease-to-own market as highly competitive with new payment products, and Four competes with other buy now pay later providers, cards and digital wallets, so pricing power is limited and approvals, not price, are the lever management uses. Buyer power sits with the large retail partners, who can renegotiate rebates, exclusivity and merchandise prices; incentive payments were USD 25.2 million in nine months, so any worse terms reduce margin directly. Substitutes are plentiful for the same customer, which limits pricing power. Entrants matter less than partner concentration. Of the macro and policy factors only two change the credit view. Economic: inflation, fuel prices, tariffs and unemployment fall on near-prime and subprime customers first and show up in write-offs within a lease term. Regulatory: state attorneys general have acted against rent-to-own disclosure, a state demand arrived in October 2026, and seven states opened a coordinated inquiry into buy now pay later providers that did not name Four, so enforcement is a recurring cost and practice risk to the core segment. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale is adequate for a niche consumer payments issuer, but the competitive position rests on partner relationships rather than a moat, and diversification is improving only in revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is good because merchandise cost and capital spending move with volume, margin stability is average because write-offs are rising, and free cash flow stability is average because conversion swung between 62.66% and 145.13% of EBITDA. Access to capital markets is adequate: the notes are priced at 95.18% of par on an estimated basis and the asset-backed notes were placed in February 2026, but no ratings were supplied. Liquidity is strong against dated obligations at USD 458.9 million, and financial policy is average because deleveraging was fast while distributions resumed. Trend: reported net leverage moved from 2.50x to 1.24x to 2.73x, and interest cover on reported EBITDA from 5.97x to 6.17x to 5.06x, so the profile is weaker than at the end of 2025 on leverage, interest cover and liquidity, although EBITDA is higher; variable-rate debt is small, a one percentage point rate change moves annual interest by about USD 0.5 million, and no hedges are used. Key missing datapoints are the covenant definitions, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and the credit agreement terms. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over 12 to 24 months the central case is flat to lower Progressive Leasing earnings with tighter approvals, stable leverage on the company definition and an accelerated repurchase that raises reported leverage. Headwinds are the cost of living and fuel prices that management cites, partner closures that continue through 2026, the tightened decisioning that management expects to pressure volume, a reduced 2026 outlook, and the covenant step-down to 3.00x in 2027; tailwinds are e-commerce growth at 26.4% of volume, improving federal employee delinquencies at Purchasing Power, Four's profit growth and the integration of Purchasing Power into one system by early 2027. Over three to five years management's growth targets to 2028 are claims, not evidence, and the more important dated event is the refinancing of the notes and revolver in November 2029, when the notes become current a year earlier. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a further consumer shock from fuel prices and unemployment, or the loss of another large retail partner. The first operational break is at Progressive Leasing: delinquencies rise, write-offs move above 8% of revenue and approvals tighten again, so volume falls and lease revenue follows with a lag of a lease term, as it already did in Q3 when volume grew and revenue did not. Financially, one extra point of write-offs on last-twelve-months Progressive Leasing revenue costs USD 22.45 million, 8.10% of reported EBITDA, and a 5% fall in that revenue at the Q3 gross margin removes USD 35.70 million of gross margin, 12.88% of reported EBITDA, before any cost response. Cash is cushioned first because a shrinking lease book releases inventory cash, which hides the earnings fall for several quarters, then the cushion fades as purchases fall with volume. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, PROG Holdings presents an adequate business profile supported by short-duration leases, low capital intensity, a recourse structure limited to USD 600.0 million of notes and liquidity of USD 458.9 million, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking and concentrated core earnings engine, rising write-offs and shareholder returns that are partly revolver funded. No peer data were supplied, so the profile cannot be benchmarked against typical leveraged consumer finance issuers. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because recent conversion was helped by inventory release and a tax refund. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Progressive Leasing earnings holding up until the notes and revolver mature in November 2029, on the covenant definition and on whether the repurchase is revolver funded. The primary downside path is partner loss or rising write-offs at Progressive Leasing feeding through to leverage while distributions continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and covenant definitions, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, partner-level concentration and the proxy statement. Top risk: erosion of Progressive Leasing earnings through partner loss or rising write-offs. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15; calculation C19

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight supplied filings and earnings supplements are enough to run the credit snapshot for PROG Holdings on primary evidence through the quarter ended September 30, 2026, but not to test covenants, security or recovery against the legal documents.

Creditors can rely on the two annual reports and three quarterly reports for debt, liquidity, covenant levels and segment results, and the newest document is 21 days old at the cutoff. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage rose sharply after the Purchasing Power acquisition: reported net debt was 2.73x LTM EBITDA at September 30, 2026, against 1.24x at the end of 2025, and creditors now share the group with USD 272.0 million of non-recourse asset-backed debt.

### Analysis by dimension

Leverage moved up because debt rose faster than EBITDA after the acquisition. Reported net debt to EBITDA was 2.50x at the end of 2024, 1.24x at the end of 2025 after the revolver draw was repaid and cash built, and 2.73x at September 30, 2026. The January 2, 2026 acquisition took about USD 391.845 million of net cash and brought USD 338.608 million of non-recourse funding debt, so carrying value debt rose to USD 865.841 million while last-twelve-months EBITDA reached only USD 277.174 million. For creditors the recourse claim is still the USD 600.0 million of notes, but the reported ratio now mixes recourse and non-recourse debt, which is why the company states 1.5x on its own definition.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C21

Interest cover on reported EBITDA slipped from 6.17x in FY2025 to 5.06x over the last twelve months. Cash interest paid rose to USD 54.727 million as asset-backed interest entered the figure, while EBITDA is struck before all interest. On the issuer adjusted measure, which treats asset-backed interest as a cost, cover is 5.85x on the same cash interest. The covenant floor is 3.00x on the facility definition, which is not the same measure and leaves headroom unestablished.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–42; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; calculation C11; calculation C13; calculation C17

Cash flow quality is steady but flattered by tax. Operating cash flow was USD 386.151 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 389.865 million a year earlier, and a swing from net tax paid of USD 46.068 million to a net refund of USD 14.614 million supplied USD 60.682 million of the comparison, so without it operating cash flow would have fallen by about USD 64.4 million. Operating cash flow is struck after USD 1,231.076 million of lease merchandise additions, so it already carries the cost of replacing the leasing inventory; capital expenditure is small at USD 13.013 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–70; calculation C24; calculation C25

Liquidity looks adequate against dated obligations. Cash of USD 108.917 million and the undrawn USD 350.0 million revolver give USD 458.917 million against no principal maturing in the printed schedule before 2029, when USD 600.0 million of notes and the revolver mature, and 2030 for the USD 272.0 million asset-backed principal. The announced USD 100.0 million share repurchase would draw on cash and the revolver, and net debt would rise by the same amount on either funding route; letters of credit under the revolver are not stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C20; calculation C23

Subsequent and multi-figure events are kept apart from period figures. The share repurchase announced on October 28, 2026 appears only in the post-balance-sheet table, and the Purchasing Power purchase price appears as USD 420.0 million negotiated, USD 424.227 million of total consideration and USD 391.845 million of net cash used, each with its role in the conflict register.

Data-quality and definition risks sit in three places. The annual and quarterly reports disagree on whether the revolver is secured, the issuer adjusted EBITDA cannot be rebuilt from readable reconciliation tables, and the cash flow statement includes discontinued operations. Customer deposits and advance payments, a non-debt funding float of USD 37.413 million at the end of 2025 against USD 40.917 million a year earlier, are kept outside debt; the balance fell during 2025 and the nine-month 2026 cash flow shows a further outflow of USD 4.073 million, which shrinks a small source of interest-free funding.

# Business & governance: PROG Holdings, Inc.
## Request

Business, transaction, ownership, operating model and governance analysis for PROG Holdings, Inc. (issuer prg-1808834), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: what the issuer does, how it is owned and financed, what changed in 2025 and 2026, and what its capital allocation behavior means for creditors.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

PROG is still a concentrated consumer-payments credit: Progressive Leasing earned 91.73% of nine-month 2026 pre-tax earnings, so the Purchasing Power acquisition has diversified revenue far more than profit. Customers of its top three retail partners generated 54.8% of 2025 consolidated revenue, and creditors hold USD 600.0 million of senior unsecured notes beside USD 272.0 million of non-recourse asset-backed debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C1

Governance risk is medium on behavior alone: PROG repaid its acquisition borrowings within six months, but it funded a USD 425.0 million tender offer with note proceeds in 2022 and has announced a USD 100.0 million accelerated share repurchase to be paid from cash and revolver borrowings, while board and ownership detail were not supplied.
### Key findings

- Partner concentration is the main business risk and has already cost volume. Customers of the top three retail partners generated 54.8% of consolidated 2025 revenue and those of the top ten 77.0%, two partners each accounted for more than 10%, and two retail partners have failed since 2024 (Big Lots in September 2024 and American Signature in November 2025), so store closures cut Progressive Leasing volume and earnings independent of customer credit quality.

- Credit performance at the core is weakening and management is trading volume for quality. Lease write-off provisions rose to 8.3% of Progressive Leasing revenue in Q3 2026 from 7.4%, above the top of the 6% to 8% annual target range, decisioning was tightened late in Q2 and again in Q3, and gross merchandise volume grew only 2.3% while revenue fell 0.7%, so tighter approvals protect losses at the cost of future revenue.

- Purchasing Power diversifies revenue but has not yet added profit. It supplied 16.88% of nine-month 2026 revenue but a pre-tax loss of USD 4.8 million, even after a USD 9.0 million fair-value gain on its receivables, and federal employee receivables, which employees may stop paying by allotment, are 9.80% of its post-acquisition accounts receivable with a past-due share of 17.35% against 12.25% for non-federal receivables.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C9

- The acquisition was funded with recourse debt that was repaid quickly, which is the clearest evidence in the documents of creditor-aligned policy. A USD 125.0 million term loan, a USD 135.0 million revolver draw and cash paid for the deal; revolver borrowings were repaid in Q1 and the term loan by June 30, 2026, and company-defined net leverage fell from about 2.5x after closing to 2.0x, 1.7x and 1.5x at the end of Q1, Q2 and Q3, at or inside the stated target range of 1.5x to 2.0x, although that measure excludes non-recourse asset-backed debt.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_prg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.2_2026-04-29_ex-992q12026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.2_2026-07-29_ex-992q22026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C19

- Shareholder returns have resumed, with one debt-funded precedent. A 2022 tender offer for USD 425.0 million was funded by note proceeds, repurchases resumed in Q2 2026 (USD 46.9 million in nine months) and the announced USD 100.0 million accelerated repurchase will use cash and revolver borrowings, but buybacks plus dividends were only 16.47% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow, so deleveraging gains can be spent on equity if the revolver share is large.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.2_2026-07-29_ex-992q22026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C13

- Ownership and board evidence is thin, so governance conclusions rest on observed behavior and on the notes' summary of creditor protections. No controlling holder is identified in the supplied documents, the audited statements carry an unqualified opinion, and the notes carry a 101% change of control put and covenants on debt, liens, distributions and affiliate transactions, but board composition, ownership percentages and covenant baskets were not supplied.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that diversification is real in growth and the new funding has performed as designed. Four grew nine-month pre-tax earnings by 359.5%, consolidated gross merchandise volume rose 58.9% in Q3, the asset-backed vehicles report covenant compliance and no early amortization event, and management says federal employee delinquencies have improved from the elevated 2025 level.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C15; calculation C20

The view would soften if Progressive Leasing write-offs returned inside the 6% to 8% range while volume recovered, if Purchasing Power reached a sustained pre-tax profit without fair-value gains, or if the proxy statement and legal documents showed strong creditor protections. It would worsen if a top three partner left, if write-offs stayed above 8%, or if revolver-funded repurchases pushed company-defined net leverage above 2.0x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.2_2026-07-29_ex-992q22026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55
### Limitations

- Partner names, contract terms and individual revenue shares are not supplied; only the top three and top ten shares and two unnamed partners above 10% are stated, so the concentration finding cannot be turned into an estimate of what the loss of one named partner would cost.

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition, control rights, executive pay and ownership percentages are not established and the medium governance rating rests on observed behavior; a controlling or activist holder would change it.

- The executed credit agreement, indenture and asset-backed documents were not supplied and the notes describe covenants without dollar baskets, so the legal room for new distributions or debt is not established and the behavior flags cannot be tied to a permitted amount.

- Purchasing Power results before January 2, 2026 are available only in a pro forma note and the purchase price allocation is preliminary, so the finding that it adds revenue but not yet profit cannot be tested against its own history.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–31; calculation C10

Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium.

The risk level is driven by a debt-funded tender offer in 2022 and a planned partly borrowed repurchase in 2026, because borrowed equity returns raise the recourse claim and use liquidity, which implies that creditor protection depends on leverage discipline that is visible today but voluntary. Countervailing evidence is the rapid repayment of the acquisition debt, company net leverage of 1.5x and the noteholders' 101% change of control put. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indenture. The governance view is complete with limitations, and the key gaps are the proxy statement, the legal documents and partner-level concentration detail.

# Fundamental credit: PROG Holdings, Inc.
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for PROG Holdings, Inc. (issuer prg-1808834), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business risk, earnings and cash conversion, leverage, liquidity, refinancing and financial policy, the strongest support and weakness, a causal downside case and the monitoring triggers.

## Findings
### Bottom line

PROG's fundamental credit is adequate but weakening: low recourse debt, short-duration leases and USD 458.9 million of liquidity protect creditors, while the core leasing profit pool is shrinking under consumer stress and cash is again being returned to shareholders.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

The recourse claim is USD 600.0 million of unsecured notes due in 2029, on which the company reports net leverage of 1.5x; on the reported basis, which also counts USD 272.0 million of non-recourse asset-backed debt, net debt to EBITDA is 2.73x at 2026-09-30 and 3.09x pro forma for the USD 100.0 million share repurchase announced on 2026-10-28. The main downside is further erosion of Progressive Leasing, which earned 91.73% of nine-month pre-tax profit, and no principal is scheduled to mature before 2029.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1; calculation C19
### Key findings

- The business profile is adequate in scale but narrow in earnings. Progressive Leasing generated 91.73% of nine-month 2026 pre-tax profit, customers of three partners produced 54.8% of 2025 revenue, and Progressive Leasing revenue fell 4.37% in the nine months while its volume grew only 1.20%, so the profit engine is shrinking even as approvals tighten.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

- Credit performance at the core is the swing factor for earnings. Write-offs rose to 8.3% of Progressive Leasing revenue in Q3 2026 from 7.4%, above the top of the 6% to 8% annual target range, Q3 Progressive Leasing pre-tax earnings fell 12.65%, and company adjusted EBITDA fell 9.50% from Q2 to Q3 2026, so group adjusted EBITDA has fallen in each quarter since Q1 2026, although seasonality may explain part of that.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C5; calculation C6

- Cash conversion is strong but flatters the trend. Operating cash flow was USD 386.2 million in the first nine months of 2026 on USD 13.0 million of capital expenditure, 166.13% of reported EBITDA, but the lease merchandise balance fell USD 97.7 million as the portfolio shrank and a tax refund replaced a tax payment, so conversion would fall if volume recovered or taxes normalised.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Leverage is low on the recourse view but rising on the reported view, and the perimeter decides the message. The company-defined ratio, which counts only the notes, is 1.53x on a house calculation, up from 1.08x at the end of 2025 because cash was spent on the acquisition, and would be 1.85x after the announced repurchase, while reported net debt to EBITDA is 2.73x at 2026-09-30 and 3.09x pro forma for the repurchase announced on 2026-10-28 because it includes the asset-backed debt and uses EBITDA before all interest.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C19; calculation C29

- Liquidity and the maturity profile give time, but 2029 is a single refinancing event. Cash of USD 108.9 million and an undrawn USD 350.0 million revolver give USD 458.9 million against no maturities until the USD 600.0 million of notes and the revolver both fall due in November 2029, and the estimated fair value of the notes slipped to 95.18% of par from 98.69% at the end of 2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C15; calculation C16

- Financial policy is the main controllable risk. The announced USD 100.0 million accelerated repurchase will use cash and revolver borrowings, equal to 21.79% of liquidity, while the leverage covenant steps down from 3.25x in 2026 to 3.00x in 2027 and 2.50x after, on a definition that was not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15; calculation C27

- Regulatory and legal exposure is a tail risk to the core that is not yet quantified. A civil investigative demand from a state attorney general arrived in October 2026, compliance duties from the 2020 consumer protection settlement continue, and a class action targets the cash advance product, while the company estimates the range of reasonably possible loss as immaterial and cannot predict outcomes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–45; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that the recourse structure is conservative and was repaid fast: USD 310.0 million of term loan and revolver borrowings were repaid within six months of the acquisition, company-defined net leverage fell from about 2.5x to 1.5x, reported EBITDA covers cash interest 5.06x, and Four's pre-tax earnings rose 359.54% in nine months. On that evidence cash generation can absorb the announced repurchase without a liquidity problem.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.2_2026-07-29_ex-992q22026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C14; calculation C21; calculation C26

The view would improve if write-offs returned inside the 6% to 8% range with Progressive Leasing revenue growing, if the repurchase were funded from cash alone, or if the credit agreement showed ample covenant headroom. It would worsen if a top three partner left, if write-offs stayed above 8%, or if the repurchase were revolver funded while company-defined net leverage moved above 2.0x; a one point rise in write-offs together with the full repurchase takes that ratio to 1.99x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; EX-99.2_2026-07-29_ex-992q22026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C20
### Limitations

- The covenant definitions were not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established and the 3.09x pro forma reported leverage cannot be read as closeness to the 3.25x or 3.00x levels; the leverage and refinancing conclusions are therefore stated on the company and reported views only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Adjusted EBITDA is stated only by the company and its reconciliation tables are unreadable, so company-defined leverage and the adjusted views rest on the company's own definition and on quarterly figures summed in Financial foundation, and the earnings trend could differ on a covenant basis.
Basis: EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The revised 2026 outlook ranges and the fourth-quarter outlook ranges are unreadable, so the 12 to 24 month view rests on the stated assumptions and the observed trend rather than on management numbers, and the direction of earnings could be better or worse than described.
Basis: EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 6

- Purchasing Power has under three quarters of history inside PROG and has not yet had a fourth quarter, so cash conversion and the leverage path after the acquisition cannot be tested through a full seasonal cycle and the first-year trend may change.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; Business & governance (CP-1A)
- No ratings, trading quotes or peer data were supplied, so the market access view rests on one estimated fair value for the notes and cannot be compared with other issuers.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Company description and credit linkage

PROG is a financial technology holding company whose profit comes mostly from one business. Progressive Leasing leases durable goods to near-prime and subprime consumers through about 24,000 partner locations and websites, and generated 91.73% of nine-month 2026 pre-tax profit and 77.70% of revenue. Purchasing Power, acquired on 2026-01-02, sells goods to employees of employer clients through payroll deduction, and Four offers buy now pay later; with the small Other segment they supplied the remaining 22.30% of revenue. Leases run for a fixed term of up to 12 months and the customer may cancel at any time by returning the merchandise, so revenue visibility is about one lease term and earnings follow approvals and partner volume quickly in both directions. The working asset is lease merchandise of USD 511.293 million and capital expenditure is only 0.59% of revenue, so cash generation depends on keeping approvals, losses and partner volume stable; that supports debt service while volume is steady and weakens it quickly when it is not.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C10
### Ownership and group structure

PROG is a listed holding company and no controlling holder is identified in the documents supplied, so no sponsor is identified that could support or extract value; Business & governance rates governance risk medium on behavior alone because the proxy statement was not supplied. The annual report says the parent depends on dividends and payments from subsidiaries, particularly Progressive Leasing, to pay debt, repurchase shares and pay dividends, which ties the notes to the earnings of the weakest-trending segment. The recourse debt is the USD 600.0 million of unsecured notes guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries that are not named; the revolver is borrowed by a subsidiary and guaranteed by the parent; and USD 272.0 million of asset-backed debt sits in non-recourse entities whose receivables are pledged, so on those assets noteholders rank behind the asset-backed lenders. The notes carry a 101% change of control put and covenants that limit debt, liens and distributions, but the baskets and the executed documents were not supplied, and the revolver is described as secured in the annual reports and unsecured in the 2026 quarterly reports, which leaves its rank unresolved.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-Q_2026-03-31_prg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38
### Revenue durability

Progressive Leasing revenue is recurring within each lease term but discretionary, cyclical and concentrated. Volume grew 1.20% in nine months and 2.3% in Q3 on a larger e-commerce share, yet revenue fell 4.37% over nine months and 0.69% in Q3 because smaller lease portfolios entered each period; active customers were flat at 781 thousand against 784 thousand. Customers of the top three partners produced 54.8% of 2025 revenue (USD 1,320.3 million) and the top ten 77.0%, partner contracts can be renegotiated or not renewed, and two retail partners have failed since 2024, so a partner event is a step-down in volume rather than a gradual drift. Management attributes the pressure to cost of living, fuel prices and the war in Iran, expects tighter decisioning to keep pressuring volume, and has reduced its 2026 revenue and earnings outlook ranges. Purchasing Power and Four are growing but small: consolidated revenue ex Purchasing Power fell 0.86% in nine months, so the group's growth is acquired.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 6; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C22; calculation C23
### Cost structure and margin resilience

The cost base is mostly variable with volume: depreciation of lease merchandise is 52.56% of nine-month consolidated revenue, so margins can be defended when volume falls, but write-offs and selling costs are less flexible. Progressive Leasing pre-tax margin was 8.13% in nine months against 8.26% a year earlier, gross margin improved to 32.4% from 31.1% because fewer customers bought early, a gain management ties to macroeconomic stress that would reverse if customers returned to early purchase, while write-offs rose. Company adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.0% in Q3 2026 against 12.3% in Q2 and 11.4% a year earlier, and reported EBITDA margin was 10.03% over the last twelve months against 9.58% in FY2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C24; calculation C25
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital expenditure is small at USD 13.0 million in nine months, but the real reinvestment is lease merchandise, which sits inside operating cash flow. Reported EBITDA converted to operating cash flow at 62.66% in FY2024, 145.13% in FY2025 and 166.13% in nine months of 2026, a spread that comes mainly from working capital and tax timing rather than earnings: the lease merchandise balance fell USD 71.2 million in FY2025 and USD 97.7 million in nine months of 2026, releasing cash as volume shrank, and net tax moved from USD 46.068 million paid in the first nine months of 2025 to USD 14.614 million received in 2026. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 324.9 million in FY2025 and USD 373.1 million in nine months of 2026, and USD 309.5 million after buybacks and dividends. The USD 310.0 million of corporate borrowings was repaid and corporate debt is back to the USD 600.0 million of notes, but cash fell from USD 308.774 million to USD 108.917 million, so net recourse debt rose by USD 199.857 million over nine months; conversion of this size is not durable, because a volume recovery would absorb cash in inventory again.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C29
### Competitive forces, macro and regulation

Competitive rivalry is high: the annual report describes the virtual lease-to-own market as highly competitive with new payment products, and Four competes with other buy now pay later providers, cards and digital wallets, so pricing power is limited and approvals, not price, are the lever management uses. Buyer power sits with the large retail partners, who can renegotiate rebates, exclusivity and merchandise prices; incentive payments were USD 25.2 million in nine months, so any worse terms reduce margin directly. Substitutes are plentiful for the same customer, which limits pricing power. Entrants matter less than partner concentration. Of the macro and policy factors only two change the credit view. Economic: inflation, fuel prices, tariffs and unemployment fall on near-prime and subprime customers first and show up in write-offs within a lease term. Regulatory: state attorneys general have acted against rent-to-own disclosure, a state demand arrived in October 2026, and seven states opened a coordinated inquiry into buy now pay later providers that did not name Four, so enforcement is a recurring cost and practice risk to the core segment.

In credit terms the strengths are low recourse debt, short lease duration, low capital intensity, liquidity with no maturity until 2029 and fixed-rate term funding for the new receivables; the weaknesses are earnings concentration in one segment, partner concentration, rising write-offs, revolver-funded shareholder returns and an unresolved covenant measure. The opportunities that could improve credit quality are Four's profit growth and a Purchasing Power move to profit; the threats that could weaken it are a top three partner exit, a consumer downturn and enforcement outcomes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is adequate for a niche consumer payments issuer, but the competitive position rests on partner relationships rather than a moat, and diversification is improving only in revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is good because merchandise cost and capital spending move with volume, margin stability is average because write-offs are rising, and free cash flow stability is average because conversion swung between 62.66% and 145.13% of EBITDA. Access to capital markets is adequate: the notes are priced at 95.18% of par on an estimated basis and the asset-backed notes were placed in February 2026, but no ratings were supplied. Liquidity is strong against dated obligations at USD 458.9 million, and financial policy is average because deleveraging was fast while distributions resumed. Trend: reported net leverage moved from 2.50x to 1.24x to 2.73x, and interest cover on reported EBITDA from 5.97x to 6.17x to 5.06x, so the profile is weaker than at the end of 2025 on leverage, interest cover and liquidity, although EBITDA is higher; variable-rate debt is small, a one percentage point rate change moves annual interest by about USD 0.5 million, and no hedges are used. Key missing datapoints are the covenant definitions, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and the credit agreement terms.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C16; calculation C19; calculation C21; calculation C28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 76
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the central case is flat to lower Progressive Leasing earnings with tighter approvals, stable leverage on the company definition and an accelerated repurchase that raises reported leverage. Headwinds are the cost of living and fuel prices that management cites, partner closures that continue through 2026, the tightened decisioning that management expects to pressure volume, a reduced 2026 outlook, and the covenant step-down to 3.00x in 2027; tailwinds are e-commerce growth at 26.4% of volume, improving federal employee delinquencies at Purchasing Power, Four's profit growth and the integration of Purchasing Power into one system by early 2027. Over three to five years management's growth targets to 2028 are claims, not evidence, and the more important dated event is the refinancing of the notes and revolver in November 2029, when the notes become current a year earlier.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 78; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.2_2026-04-29_ex-992q12026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a further consumer shock from fuel prices and unemployment, or the loss of another large retail partner. The first operational break is at Progressive Leasing: delinquencies rise, write-offs move above 8% of revenue and approvals tighten again, so volume falls and lease revenue follows with a lag of a lease term, as it already did in Q3 when volume grew and revenue did not. Financially, one extra point of write-offs on last-twelve-months Progressive Leasing revenue costs USD 22.45 million, 8.10% of reported EBITDA, and a 5% fall in that revenue at the Q3 gross margin removes USD 35.70 million of gross margin, 12.88% of reported EBITDA, before any cost response. Cash is cushioned first because a shrinking lease book releases inventory cash, which hides the earnings fall for several quarters, then the cushion fades as purchases fall with volume. On the reported basis a one point rise in write-offs lifts net debt to EBITDA from 2.73x to 2.97x, and to 3.36x with the full repurchase; on the company definition the same two events give 1.99x, at the top of the 1.5x to 2.0x range, and cover on reported EBITDA falls to 4.65x. Liquidity of USD 458.9 million, no maturity before 2029 and USD 36.0 million of annual note interest mean distress is unlikely within 12 to 24 months; management levers are to cancel the repurchase, cut lease merchandise purchases, sell charged-off receivables and cut costs. The observable triggers are write-offs above 8% for a second quarter, a partner exit, a revolver draw, a rising notes discount and any change in covenant compliance language.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C20; calculation C24; calculation C15; calculation C18
### Overall credit view

Overall, PROG Holdings presents an adequate business profile supported by short-duration leases, low capital intensity, a recourse structure limited to USD 600.0 million of notes and liquidity of USD 458.9 million, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking and concentrated core earnings engine, rising write-offs and shareholder returns that are partly revolver funded. No peer data were supplied, so the profile cannot be benchmarked against typical leveraged consumer finance issuers. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because recent conversion was helped by inventory release and a tax refund. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Progressive Leasing earnings holding up until the notes and revolver mature in November 2029, on the covenant definition and on whether the repurchase is revolver funded. The primary downside path is partner loss or rising write-offs at Progressive Leasing feeding through to leverage while distributions continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and covenant definitions, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, partner-level concentration and the proxy statement. Top risk: erosion of Progressive Leasing earnings through partner loss or rising write-offs.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15; calculation C19
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths, ranked by weight in the credit view:

- Low recourse leverage that was cut fast. The recourse claim is USD 600.0 million of notes and the company reports 1.5x net leverage after repaying USD 310.0 million of corporate borrowings within six months of the acquisition, which supports probability of default and recovery for the notes while that discipline lasts, although company-defined leverage is above the 1.08x of the end of 2025 because cash funded part of the acquisition.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C14; calculation C19; calculation C29

- Liquidity with no maturity before 2029. Cash of USD 108.9 million and an undrawn USD 350.0 million revolver total USD 458.9 million, no principal falls due until November 2029 and annual note interest is USD 36.0 million, so a near-term liquidity event would need a severe earnings collapse.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C15; calculation C18

- Capital-light cash generation. Capital expenditure is 0.59% of revenue and nine-month operating cash flow of USD 386.2 million funded debt repayment and distributions, which supports debt service, although part of it is a release of lease inventory.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Ring-fenced term funding for Purchasing Power receivables. USD 272.0 million of non-recourse asset-backed notes mature in 2030 at a weighted fixed coupon of 4.87% on the 2026 series and report no early amortization event, which keeps that funding off the corporate liquidity line while performance holds.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C17

- Short lease duration. Leases run up to 12 months and cancel at any time, so loss experience shows quickly and the company can tighten approvals within a quarter, as it did late in Q2 and again in Q3, which protects the portfolio at the cost of volume.
Weaknesses, ranked by weight in the credit view:

- Earnings concentration in a shrinking core. Progressive Leasing produced 91.73% of nine-month pre-tax profit while its revenue fell 4.37%, so group debt service depends on the segment whose volume and write-offs are moving the wrong way.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C1; calculation C3

- Partner concentration. Customers of the top three partners produced 54.8% of 2025 revenue and two partners have failed since 2024, so a single partner event cuts volume with no contractual revenue floor because leases are cancellable.

- Rising write-offs. Provisions reached 8.3% of Progressive Leasing revenue against 7.4%, above the 6% to 8% annual target, and each extra point costs about USD 22.45 million of EBITDA, so earnings are sensitive to consumer stress.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C20

- Revolver-funded shareholder returns. The announced USD 100.0 million repurchase uses cash and revolver borrowings and lifts reported net debt to EBITDA to 3.09x, while buybacks and dividends were 16.47% of nine-month operating cash flow, so distributions compete with deleveraging.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C19

- Unresolved covenant and refinancing position. The leverage covenant steps down from 3.25x to 3.00x in 2027 and 2.50x after on an unsupplied definition, and the notes and revolver both fall due in November 2029 with the notes estimated at 95.18% of par, so headroom and market access are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C16; calculation C27
